catalog.summary: Start and end times with a picker.

valueRules.empty: a request whose both ends are null carries null; the family speaks one word for nothing
valueRules.openEnd: { start, end: null } and { start: null, end } are values: an open end is written in the field, where the reader sees it
valueRules.reversed: an end typed before its start is invalid and stays as typed
valueRules.midnight: a shift from 22:00 to 06:00 is an end before its start: a PlainTime has no day, and a run that crosses midnight has two of them. datetime-range-picker is the family that writes it.

pattern.title: Listbox Pattern, for the list; Tabs Pattern, for the two ends; Date Picker Dialog Example, for the popup
pattern.rangePattern: none exists; the dialog example for the popup, the tabs pattern for the two ends and the listbox pattern for the list, as time-picker
pattern.departure: the dialog example closes on the first press and this family closes when the work is whole, because a range is at least two presses; closeOnSelect names the rest

panel.current: one panel, the current end's: the list of that end, refusing what the other end of the work refuses
panel.labelledBy: the current tab, so a screen reader hears "Start, 14:00" before the first option
panel.why: One end at a time. Two lists side by side, under two fields, were refused at the release gate as too much interface at once for a lay reader and for a phone: two lists of ninety-six rows with 32-pixel targets, a full-screen sheet with no way out, nested scrolling. The tab says which end, the panel shows only that end, and choosing one end moves to the other; the end list appears already striking what the chosen start refuses, in the same gesture.
panel.reversed: the first contract declined "one list that swaps with the position, as MUI and Ant ship" because what the start refuses of the end was discovered only after switching; the switch is now automatic at the moment the start is chosen, and the argument fell

list.shape: time-picker's list, unchanged: step, options, maxOptions, min, max, isTimeUnavailable, unavailableOptions
list.otherEnd: the end list refuses the options before the start, those whose duration falls outside minLength and maxLength, and with contiguous those beyond the first unavailable option after the start; the start list refuses the options after the end, the same length rule, and those before the first unavailable option before the end
list.refusedDrawn: a refused option is still drawn with aria-disabled, or hidden with unavailableOptions=hide, the rule of time-picker
list.duration: each option in the list of one end carries, beside its time, the duration the run would have with the other end as it stands — "15:00 · 1 hr" — the way a calendar application lists the end times of an event; a refused option carries none. The band's length says the same for the pending end, in a live region, so a screen reader hears what the rows show.

focusRule.rule: the press that leaves the work incomplete carries focus to the end that is missing, swapping the tab to it; the press that completes the work closes the panel
focusRule.whole: with the work already whole, a press writes the value and the panel stays open; focus stays where the reader put it

draft.rule: while the panel is open the family holds the work: the two ends as the reader left them. A press that leaves the work with one end emits no value; the press that completes it emits the whole run with reason select, and every later press that changes a whole work emits again
draft.abandonedBy: Escape, an outside press and the trigger abandon the work and keep the previous value
draft.openEndValue: a panel opened over { start, end: null } opens on the end tab with that work, and the first press in the list completes it

length.pending: the duration of the run that would exist if the pending end were chosen — the option under the pointer, or the highlighted option of the list that has focus — with the other end taken from the work; with no pending end, the duration of the work
length.unit: seconds between the two ends, turned into words
length.label: durationLabel(seconds, locale, granularity) from @slotted/core/date by default, replaceable per instance and per provider as lengthLabel(seconds, locale)
length.sameTime: the same time at both ends is 0 min, and the band says so

highlight.shape: { start: PlainTime | null, end: PlainTime | null }: the highlighted option of each list
highlight.why: One model for two lists, because the two are one capability — where the reader is — and a family holding two current models would be two names for one place. The option under the pointer is not the highlight: it enters length and nothing else.

position.meaning: the end whose tab carries aria-selected and data-current, whose field and panel are shown, and which focus enters when the panel opens
position.onOpen: the first end that is missing; with a whole value, where it was
position.afterTab: the pressed end, reason pointer or keyboard
position.afterNow: the rule of a list press

now.writes: the current time into the current end, and follows the focus rule
now.equals: the zero case of time-field's relative expression
now.why: one now, because one end is shown at a time

step.base: min when it is stated, midnight when it is not
step.source: the platform's own rule for input[type=time], where the step base is min if specified, the value otherwise, and 0 if neither
step.floorReason: A step finer than a minute is a real configuration: thirty-second slots inside a five-minute window is eleven rows. A floor of one minute was written at the visual gate and withdrawn on the reviewer's reading — it refused the window along with the day it was aimed at. The guard belongs on the length of the list, which is maxOptions, and not on the size of the step.
step.offStepReason: A step of 900 with min 09:07 offers 09:07, 09:22, 09:37. The field still accepts 09:15 by typing, and the family reports invalid only when a bound or the predicate refuses the value — never because it fell between two options.
step.notTheFieldArrows: The panel's step is the panel's. A segment steps by one of its own unit and pages by the page step, whatever the panel offers. input[type=time] ties the two and this family does not: a minute arrow that moved fifteen at a time would put :07 out of reach of the arrows, and the field's promise is that every value is reachable there.

selectionFollowsFocusReason: The listbox pattern lists it as optional and warns it can degrade accessibility. Here a reader arrowing through ninety-six quarter-hours would emit ninety-six requests; the highlight moves, and Enter, Space or a press moves the work.

limits.crossed: the start field and list take max = min(max, end); the end field and list take min = max(min, start)

contiguous.list: with a start chosen, the options beyond the first unavailable option after it are refused in the end list; with an end chosen, the options before the first unavailable option before it are refused in the start list
contiguous.search: over the list, once per chosen end, never over the seconds: a list holds at most maxOptions entries
contiguous.typed: the predicate runs over the two typed ends once per value change

limits.explained: the limit part names minLength and maxLength while either is set, through the limit.between, limit.atLeast and limit.atMost messages, each duration written by lengthLabel

validity.owned: bounds, unavailable times, the order of the two ends, and the duration
validity.reversed: an end before its start is invalid on the end field and on the frame; the ends are not swapped

clear.fields: the two fields do not draw their own clear; one button on the frame empties both ends with reason clear

preset.value: a TimeRange, or a function returning one, resolved on press
preset.invalid: a preset whose range fails a rule still writes it and the value is invalid; the preset is not hidden

wiring.aria-expanded: the trigger, while the popup is showing
wiring.aria-controls: the content, while the popup is showing
wiring.aria-label: the trigger, carrying both ends and the duration

triggerName.chosen: the change message, with both ends in words and the duration in its start, end and length slots; changeReversed, without the duration, while the ends are out of order
triggerName.why: Focus returns to the trigger when the popup closes, so the name is where the reader is told what was chosen.

keyboard.focusTo: the first segment of the current end's field, or its list where the field is not drawn
the list of the current end, on its time or on the nearest offered step

keyboard.effect: the other tab, with automatic activation: position moves and the panel swaps
time-field's, unchanged, the relative expression included

keyboard.key: ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home, End, PageDown, PageUp, a-z0-9
keyboard.effect: time-picker's list keys: the next or previous option, the first or last, one hour, type-ahead; each move is the pending end and length says the duration
writes the current end; then the focus rule
close, emitting a whole work first

keyboard.staged: the relative expression of the field first; then the panel closes and the work is abandoned

keyboard.sequence: the tabs (one stop), the field, now, presets, the list, footer, done

platformNotes.altArrowDown: ChromeOS turns Alt+ArrowDown into PageDown before the browser sees it, which Angular Material records for its own input. The trigger button is therefore the guaranteed path and the chord is a shortcut, never the only way in.

dismissal.escape: through dismissable-layer, in the capture phase
dismissal.closeOnSelect: auto closes when the work becomes whole, by a press in a list, by now or by a preset; always closes on any press that changes the value; never closes on none

branches: the trigger, so pressing it again closes rather than dismissing and reopening

responsive.sheet: below 480px on a coarse pointer, the content takes the sheet presentation
responsive.decidedIn: the stylesheet; the DOM does not change
responsive.coarsePointer: the rows and the tabs stand at the control height the theme raises to --slotted-target-comfortable; the field is not drawn
responsive.sheetList: six rows and a half, the only thing that scrolls; the content is capped at 100dvh and scrolls as one when it does not fit, ending with the safe-area inset and done
responsive.presets: a wrapping row of chips between the head and the panel, at every width

portalledIdentity.reason: The family is two subtrees: the control where the consumer wrote it, and the popup portalled to the end of the document. A stylesheet cannot reach a subtree that is no longer inside the root, so data-ui is written on both.

forms.angular: ControlValueAccessor writes the whole TimeRange; Validator reports the family's own errors
forms.hiddenInputs: two, on the frame, because the panel in a portal is not inside the form while it is closed

dataAttributes.data-position: on a tab, the field and the panel: start or end
dataAttributes.data-granularity: hour, minute or second, on the root
dataAttributes.data-truncated: on a list: it stops short of the times the configuration asked for, at maxOptions
dataAttributes.data-placement: the side and alignment the positioner resolved
dataAttributes.data-placeholder: on summary and on a tab: there is no value and the text is the placeholder
dataAttributes.data-pending: on length: what is shown is the duration for the pending end, not the work

statePrecedence.guard: every weaker rule carries a :not() for each stronger state it can meet, because specificity rather than source order is what decides between them — the rule time-picker recorded at its visual gate

literals.--slotted-time-range-picker-sheet-inline: 100%, which the shared exemption list already holds.
literals.--slotted-time-range-picker-list-block-s: Eight rows and half of the ninth, counted in the row height the panel states once — the literal time-picker records, for the same reason: a list cut on a row boundary looks like the whole list.

control.shape: one line at the control height: the value written short in the locale, or the placeholder, cut with an ellipsis when it does not fit, a clear, and the trigger that fills the frame
control.why: two time fields in one frame need about 220 pixels on one line, a segment cannot shrink, and below that the frame broke into two lines against the control height every form counts on. Withdrawn at the visual gate on the reviewer's reading
control.fullName: the trigger carries both ends in words and the duration, so the ellipsis removes nothing a reader cannot hear

head.holds: three rows: the two tabs; the current end's field and now; the hint, then the length and the limit
head.current: data-current and aria-selected on the current tab, painted whenever the panel is open
head.fieldsSubmit: the field carries no name; the two hidden-input parts on the frame submit startName and endName

tabs.tab: role="tab" on a button, one per end, carrying tab-label and tab-value; aria-selected and data-current on the current end; data-placeholder while the end has no value
tabs.activation: automatic: ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home and End move position with reason keyboard; a press moves it with reason pointer
tabs.value: the end written short in the locale, or a dash

hint.says: what the next press should be, or what is wrong: choose while the current end is missing; order, length, unavailable or bounds while the work is whole and invalid; empty while the work is whole and valid, when length says the duration
hint.messages: chooseTime, with {end} for the end's name; order, length, unavailable, bounds
hint.wiring: aria-describedby of the list and of the field
hint.why: a panel that only refuses — struck rows, a red frame — does not say what can be done; the hint does

done.label: the done message
done.effect: closes with reason pointer; a whole work is emitted with reason select before closing; one end alone stays as it is
done.why: a sheet that fills the screen has no outside to press and no Escape key; on the desktop it is the way out of an edit left half way

field.one: the current end's time-field in variant plain, under the tabs, with now beside it
field.finePointerOnly: a segment is a spinbutton, not an input, and raises no keyboard on a phone; the stylesheet does not draw the field under (pointer: coarse)
field.writes: the current end of the work at every request the field emits, with the field's reason; a whole work is emitted as the value
